external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are
external_entities.notes: The description does not state where colleagues are located or whether they are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who signs in through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for their identities.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The description does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system from which the identity broker obtains overnight changes to group membership and colleague status.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, supplies public signing-key material, and consumes directory and HR changes.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The description does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses token groups to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the key store is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what that log records, whether it covers the franchise route, or whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in through the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through the identity broker using a vouch from the franchise identity provider.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The description does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token containing a colleague's staff ID and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: token carrying the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a franchise colleague after accepting the identity-provider sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The description does not explicitly state whether the franchise token has the same contents as other tokens.

data_flows.name: change prices and void transactions
data_flows.description: A colleague presents a token to the store admin console, which permits price changes and transaction voids when the token has the store-manager group.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.
data_flows.data_description: token with staff id and group membership; price and transaction administration

data_flows.name: change prices and void transactions
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague uses a token with the store-manager group at the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The description does not explicitly state that franchise colleagues use the store admin console.

data_flows.name: fetch public half
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the token-signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: keep signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps the token-signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: keep membership
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps colleagues and their group memberships in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls overnight group-membership and colleague-status changes from the HR system.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The same overnight pull is how leavers stop being colleagues.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The description does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home devices
trust_boundaries.description: Colleagues' own devices at home from which they may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise identity provider
trust_boundaries.description: The separate trust zone controlled by the franchise identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it stores colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory stores colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The signing key store's contents are confidential because it stores the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds the signing key used to sign tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's contents are confidential because it stores sign-in events associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
